## What's new

Threadnote 5.4.0 makes development workflows up to 45× faster, adds a lighter default dev-cycle profile, moves semantic reads into native code, makes code-graph indexing and checkpoints much cheaper on large repositories, and stops background maintenance from using CPU all the time.

### Faster development workflows

Every dev-cycle command now stays responsive on a large checkout and memory corpus. Measured on a 105,000-file checkout with about 5,300 memories:

| Command                                     | 5.3.8                      | 5.4.0     | Change       |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | --------- | ------------ |
| `task-start`, first start of a compact task | 298 s                      | 6.6 s     | −97.8%       |
| `compact-confirm`                           | 104 s                      | 5.4–9.9 s | −90% to −95% |
| `remember` of one new memory                | 95 s                       | 1.6–1.9 s | −98%         |
| `task-view`                                 | 1.0 s                      | 0.44 s    | −56%         |
| `record-snapshot` on a clean tree           | stash, restore and retries | 1.3–1.7 s | no retries   |

### A lighter default dev-cycle profile

New runs use the `standard` profile. It gates only on intent and review integrity, so routine bookkeeping no longer blocks work:

- The newest snapshot of a tree supersedes any unreviewed one.
- Phase ownership is derived from the plan. Files outside the plan produce warnings, not refusals.
- A review is reused when the change is byte-identical, and incremental review is the default.
- Every refusal names the failing gate and the exact `next` command, from both the CLI and MCP.
- Review gates can be waived only with recorded authority.
- A task starts in a new worktree without a ready code graph. The graph indexes in the background. A start that had to wait for a full index now returns in about 9 s.
- Files outside the plan are advisory at every gate, and closeout records the actual changed files.

The `strict` profile keeps the previous behavior, including a ready graph at start, and runs already on disk stay strict.

### More reliable workflows and memory

- `record-review` says which findings break the prior-identity rule and how to report them, so agents no longer retry blind.
- A workflow run resumes after its home or checkout moves behind a link. A copied home or another clone is still refused.
- A run written by a newer Threadnote reports a version mismatch that names both versions, instead of calling the state malformed.
- `watch-pr` can wake Claude Code sessions as well as Cursor.
- `watch-pr` with only a PR URL always starts a monitor-only watch, whatever the workflow state. A later workflow watch for the same PR replaces it.
- Closeout accepts a merged PR whose head moved past a phase head, such as a multi-phase PR or one with pushes after delivery. `watch-pr renew --recoverWakeup` clears a wake that a reinstall interrupted.
- `record-snapshot` can replace a blocked review target, so a run no longer deadlocks after two invalid review records. Snapshot and review refusals are bounded and name what is missing.
- PR delivery and `watch-pr` work in clones whose remote has no fetch mapping, or that reach GitHub through an SSH host alias such as `git@github.com-work:`. When the PR base can't be verified, the error now names the failing check and, where one exists, the command that fixes it.
- A task started from a second worktree uses the repository's identity, not its folder name, and a refused start writes nothing.
- Handoff saves always end in an explained state. A save that could not start says why and that a retry is safe.
- `remember_context` accepts compact `memories/...` pointers in `replaceUri`, and deferred citations work when replacing a memory.
- `recall_context` with only `memoryRefs` returns connections with a stale-index warning instead of nothing.
- Large recall reads no longer fail when refinement output passes 16 MiB, and `lexical_read_failed` names a reason and a fix.
- A background code-anchor heal no longer makes a memory write fail with `memory-busy`.
- `context_brief` ranks declarations above modules that match only by path, and a stale index brief recommends `graph-status` first.
- A `context_brief` locate brief keeps retrieved memories when the graph has no evidence or its read times out. Before, it returned no evidence.
- Semantic vectors that were queued before a structural reindex stay queued, instead of reporting `not-requested`.
- `read_context` returns the memory body in Claude Code.
- `repair` and memory writes no longer fail with `SQLITE_BUSY` while another process rebuilds lexical recall, and `repair` retries when concurrent writes supersede its lexical preparation.
- Dev skill links to `references/writing.md` resolve in installed skills.
- `tn` is now a managed short alias for `threadnote`. An existing `tn` that Threadnote did not write is left alone.

### Lower background CPU

Automatic context maintenance could run most of the time. One 5.3.8 install ran the maintenance worker for 69% of wall-clock time over 8 days. In 5.4.0:

- Quiet maintenance ticks back off from 30 s up to 30 minutes, and wake again when memory changes or a retry is due.
- A tick reads only the ready lexical snapshot and does not wake embedding workers.
- MCP server startup throttles its deferred code-anchor refresh per home, so a server that restarts every 5 minutes no longer repeats that work.

### Faster code graph

- **Export edits.** An edit that adds, removes or renames an exported name reads a persisted reverse reference index instead of rebuilding the graph. On a 3,600-file repository a later edit takes 2.86 s instead of 130.7 s (−97.8%). On a 100,000-file fixture it takes 13.0 s instead of 155 s (−91.6%).
- **Stored-fact decoding.** Native decompression decodes stored facts in 764 ms instead of 8,084 ms (−90.5%). Faster validation then removes another 29.5% from fact decoding and 21% from the replay stage of a full index.
- **Checkpoints.** Checkpoint chunks decode 96–97% faster and encode 82% faster, and new checkpoints are about 10% smaller. A large-repository export takes 89.7 s instead of 133.4 s (−32.8%).
- **Checkpoint export fixes.** Export works for repositories whose `tsconfig.json` has comments or trailing commas, and for large repositories whose graph was built without checkpoint shards. The first export of such a repository rebuilds the graph once.

### Native semantic reads

Semantic vector reads now run in Rust on every release target. On Apple silicon, warm reads are faster at p95: 23–26% at 100,000 dense vectors, about 19% at 100,000 tied vectors, and about 10% at 10,000. Peak memory is 3–4% lower. The first read after startup at 10,000 vectors is slower, because it loads the native reader.

The ready-read worker now starts before the rest of the CLI loads. Its p99 latency on Intel Macs drops from 987 ms to 701 ms (−29%), and its startup on Apple silicon from 59 ms to 43 ms (−27%).

Local embeddings no longer crash on Windows ARM.

### Before you upgrade

- **Checkpoints.** New checkpoints and shared graph deltas use the `threadnote-gzip-v2` format. Earlier releases reject them, so upgrade receivers before importing from 5.4.0. This release still imports older checkpoints.
- **Workflow runs and PR watches.** Once 5.4.0 writes a workflow run, PR watch or delivery receipt, earlier releases refuse it. Finish or abandon a run before rolling back.
- **One-time rebuilds.** The lexical recall index and the code-graph store upgrade on first use. Lexical recall rebuilds once from your memory files.

Dependencies are updated, including Effect 4.1.4, and all security advisories with an available fix are resolved.
